_comment: Findings `blocktracer-rehearse` produces TODAY, against the corpus `just rehearse` gives it,
with the reason, the cause from readings, the subject that would close it, and who can build
that subject.
THIS FILE FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, like `tools/journeys/known-survivors.json` beside it and
`ci/test/ci-coverage.known-dark.txt` one directory over. A registered finding that OCCURS is
reported and does not fail the run. A registered finding that does NOT occur fails the run by
name, demanding the entry be deleted — so an entry cannot outlive the defect it records, and
nobody has to remember to clean up after closing one. An UNREGISTERED finding fails.
AN ENTRY IS ONLY LEGITIMATE WITH ALL SIX FIELDS, and `rehearse/register.nim` refuses the whole
register rather than reading around a missing one:
reason    — what the rehearsal found, in its own terms
cause     — WHY it happens, from readings and not from inference
subject   — what would make it stop happening, concretely enough to go and build
closed_by — who can produce that subject, and where the work lives
evidence  — what was measured, when, and on what tree
recorded  — the date this entry was written, so the debt is dated and not merely present
THE REGISTER IS TIED TO A CORPUS. Every entry here is about the tree `just rehearse` runs over
— the demo generator's output. A rehearsal over a different corpus legitimately produces
different findings, and running one with this register will fail on the difference in both
directions, which is the correct answer and not a bug: a register is evidence about a specific
measurement, not a global list of things that are allowed to be wrong. `just rehearse-tree DIR`
takes no register for exactly that reason.
NOT LEGITIMATE HERE: a finding that occurs because the rehearsal itself is wrong. Three such
were produced and fixed rather than registered while this tool was being written (a top-level
static directory read as a chain, an off-by-one in a generation path index, and a substring
test that could not tell `demo` from `demo-rehearsal-b`). A register whose bar is set after it
is already long gets the bar its longest-serving entries deserve.
COUNT THE KEYS IN `known_findings`; do not trust a sentence here saying how many there are.

coverage/class/ocAsset.reason: `publisher.classOf` returns `ocAsset` for a key under `assets/` or `_a/`, and the demo generator emits no such key, so a rehearsal over its output never writes one. The asset class's upload path is therefore unexercised by this corpus, and the rehearsal refuses to call itself sufficient rather than reporting 35/36.
coverage/class/ocAsset.cause: Measured, not inferred: `grep -rn 'assets/' src/blocktracer/` matches ONLY `publisher.nim`'s two lines — the `classOf` arm and the `belongs` arm. Nothing under `src/blocktracer/demo/` or `src/blocktracer/chain/` ever writes an `assets/**` key. The site's assets come from a different producer: `tools/deploy/check-assets.mjs` names `/assets/hydrate.js` as the hydration bundle's URL, and the built tree at `client/dist` carries `assets/hydrate.js` and `assets/fonts/*.woff2`. So the class is real and has a producer; that producer is the client export step, which `blocktracer-demo-gen` is not.
coverage/class/ocAsset.subject: A corpus that includes the tree actually published. `just rehearse-tree client/dist` after `just export-hydrated` covers it — measured on 2026-09-29 over a built 878-object `client/dist`, where `class/ocAsset` is met by `assets/fonts/SpaceGrotesk-Bold.woff2` and the run reaches 36/36. The debt is that `just rehearse` cannot build that tree in the `contract` CI job, which has no client build.
coverage/class/ocAsset.closed_by: Whoever moves the rehearsal into a lane that already holds a built site — `deploy-cloudflare-pages.yml` stages one at `site/` and runs `check-assets.mjs --dir site` against it — or adds an asset-bearing fixture to the demo generator. The first is preferable: it rehearses the bytes that are about to be uploaded, which is the same argument `check-assets.mjs` makes about itself.
coverage/class/ocAsset.evidence: 2026-09-29, worktree `blocktracer-rehearsal-modes` at `origin/dev` 81e1886. `blocktracer-rehearse --tree <demo-gen output> --mode partial`: 35/36 cells, `class/ocAsset` MISS. The same binary over a copy of `client/dist` (878 objects, 106 rehearsed): 36/36, `class/ocAsset` met with witness `A1: assets/fonts/SpaceGrotesk-Bold.woff2`.

invariant/global-pointer-no-chain-loss.reason: Publishing a second single-chain producer tree into a store that already holds another chain leaves `registry/chains.v1.json` naming only the second chain, while the first chain's objects remain in the store. The registry is the only object that lists a chain, so that chain becomes present and invisible to every reader. This is the 2026-09-28 data-loss defect, and it is still live on `dev`.
invariant/global-pointer-no-chain-loss.cause: `registry/**` classifies as `ocPointer`, whose strategy is `stUnconditional` — always rewrite — and the key carries no chain segment, so every chain's cycle writes the same key. `ingest.nim` does merge a registry, but it merges WITHIN one tree; two chains ingested into two trees each produce a registry holding one chain and the second publish overwrites the first. Reproduced directly with the shipped CLI, not only through the rehearsal: publish the demo tree, then publish a tree re-keyed onto a second slug, and `registry/chains.v1.json` lists one chain while `d/` holds two directories.
invariant/global-pointer-no-chain-loss.subject: Either a publisher that REFUSES a tree whose registry drops a chain the store already holds, or a pipeline that ingests every chain into one shared tree so `ingest.nim`'s merge sees them all. Both make this rehearsal green: the invariant is stated over the store's contents after the sequence, so a refusal satisfies it and a correct merge satisfies it, and only writing-and-losing does not.
invariant/global-pointer-no-chain-loss.closed_by: The publish-path work in progress on `bt/full-history-backfill`, which adds `assertRegistryKeepsKnownChains` and `assertNoUnknownGlobalPointer` to `publishTree`. Those procs are NOT on `dev` at the time of writing — `git grep` finds them on that branch only. When they land, this entry must be deleted, and the rehearsal will demand the deletion by name on the first run after the merge.
invariant/global-pointer-no-chain-loss.evidence: 2026-09-29, worktree `blocktracer-rehearsal-modes` at `origin/dev` 81e1886, against a local object store. From a 54-object PARTIAL rehearsal of the 310-object demo tree, and again from a 106-object partial rehearsal of the 878-object `client/dist`. The full-scale rehearsal that first found it on 2026-09-28 used 460,589 objects; the defect needs cardinality 2, not scale.
